t: For research and development activities, $233,568,000, to remain available until September 30, 1981.

fable.w: This section is a bare appropriation of funds for research and development activities with a period of availability. It names no outside party, consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision. The only tempting reading is that research might involve outside experts, but the text says nothing of the kind.

opus.w: The section only appropriates $233,568,000 for research and development activities and sets how long the money stays available. No one outside the federal government is involved: there is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. Like Example 1, it is just a funding provision.
opus.b: This is a plain appropriation of money. Nothing in it involves outside parties, consultation, hearings, advisory boards, rulemaking, or a right to sue. The word "research" might seem to hint at outside involvement, but no outside party or decision process is mentioned.

qwen_chat.w: This provision is a standard appropriations clause specifying the amount of funding and its availability period. It does not mention any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties, nor does it establish any advisory bodies or public comment periods.
qwen_chat.s: For research and development activities, $233,568,000, to remain available until September 30, 1981.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: Nothing. The text is purely about funding levels and availability dates.
Resolution: This provision is a standard appropriations clause. It does not mention any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties.
